themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Accumulation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: CD207 experienced a severe spike in dead animal complaints THIS WEEK: 15 complaints vs. 1.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (1400% increase, z-score 14.0), suggesting either a disease outbreak, environmental contamination event, or systemic failure in animal removal services.
evidence: 15 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1400% spike)
Z-score of 14.0 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Timing coincides with seasonal weather or potential disease cluster
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about response capacity and whether a specific event (disease, contamination) triggered the spike
Canvass residents in blocks with multiple complaints to document location patterns and health concerns

themes_detail.label: Uncontrolled Cannabis Retail Expansion
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 8 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score 9.9), indicating rapid unauthorized or nuisance retail operations opening in the district without community oversight.
evidence: 8 cannabis retailer complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 9.9 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Suggests either rapid illegal storefronts or licensed retailers causing neighborhood friction
reporting_angles: Map the 8 complaints by address to identify clusters and check licensing status against SCA records
Interview community board about whether retail expansion was part of any approved plan or if complaints reflect unlicensed operations

themes_detail.label: Park Wildlife Disturbances Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints spiked to 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase, z-score 8.69), suggesting either a wildlife intrusion event or new hazard in public green spaces affecting resident safety and park usability.
evidence: 3 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Timing suggests acute event rather than chronic condition
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to identify which parks are affected and whether wildlife management action has been taken
Interview residents on which animals were sighted and whether they felt safety risk in public spaces

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints nearly quadrupled to 5 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% increase, z-score 5.67), pointing to either a cluster of inspection failures, foodborne illness reports, or sanitation violations in restaurants or street vendors.
evidence: 5 food establishment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (300% spike)
Z-score of 5.67 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Could indicate either single outbreak source or distributed compliance failures
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 5 complaints with DOHMH inspection records to identify specific violations and business names
Interview Department of Health about whether complaints cluster around one establishment or reflect broader sanitation breakdown

themes_detail.label: Street Obstruction & Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction and curb condition complaints combined show significant spikes LAST WEEK (7 obstruction complaints vs. 1.9 average; curb condition spike 3 weeks ago), indicating accumulating street-level infrastructure failure and debris that may pose pedestrian hazards and traffic disruption.
evidence: 7 obstruction complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (273% spike, z-score 5.53)
Curb condition spike of 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 average (2300% increase, z-score 8.69)
Combined signal suggests systemic street maintenance lag
reporting_angles: Map obstruction complaints by location to identify whether specific corridors or blocks are neglected
File FOIL request to Sanitation for street sweeping schedules in CD207 to assess coverage gaps
